definitions.explanation: A painter who designed ukiyo-e, the prints and paintings of everyday life, actors, beauties, and landscapes popular in the Edo period.

examples.japanese: ⟦{有名|ゆうめい}→有名：01106_yuumei⟧な{浮世絵師|うきよえし}。
{北斎|ほくさい}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{江戸|えど}{時代|じだい}→江戸時代：20431_edojidai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{浮世絵師|うきよえし}だ。
examples.english: Hokusai was an ukiyo-e artist of the Edo period.

examples.japanese: {浮世絵師|うきよえし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{描|か}いた→描く：28436_kaku⟧{下絵|したえ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧もと⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧、{彫師|ほりし}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{摺師|すりし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{版画|はんが}→版画：10582_hanga⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{仕上|しあ}げた→仕上げる：04664_shiageru⟧。
examples.english: Carvers and printers finished the prints from the designs drawn by the ukiyo-e artist.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
⟦{浮世絵|うきよえ}→浮世絵：13286_ukiyoe⟧ (ukiyo-e) + {師|し} (master of a craft).

CULTURAL NOTE:
A print was a team effort: the {浮世絵師|うきよえし} drew the design, a {彫師|ほりし} carved the blocks, a {摺師|すりし} printed them, and a publisher ({版元|はんもと}) financed and sold the result. Famous names include ⟦{葛飾北斎|かつしかほくさい}→葛飾北斎：31024_katsushikahokusai⟧, {歌川広重|うたがわひろしげ}, and {喜多川歌麿|きたがわうたまろ}.

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{絵師|えし}→絵師：13878_eshi⟧: painter (premodern; today also an illustrator)
- ⟦{画家|がか}→画家：02583_gaka⟧: painter, artist (the general modern word)
